scope: Figures to assign each simulated US resident a health coverage status from age, job, employer size, household income relative to the poverty line, and state; plus totals to check the result. Percentages are percent (0-100). Income limits are percent of the federal poverty level (FPL) for the household size.

sources.title: KFF State Health Facts: Medicaid Income Eligibility Limits for Adults as a Percent of the FPL; Medicaid and CHIP Income Eligibility Limits for Children; ... for Pregnant Women
sources.notes: Only timeframe the live pages publish. Based on the KFF / Georgetown University Center for Children and Families annual 50-state survey. Limits are MAGI-converted and include the 5-percentage-point FPL disregard (so ACA expansion shows as 138). Parents are % of FPL for a family of three; other adults for an individual. Values parsed from the data embedded in each page. Children 'children' = KFF 'Upper Income Limit' (highest Medicaid or CHIP limit for any child 0-18). Pregnant = higher of the Medicaid and CHIP pregnancy columns; the FCEP (unborn-child CHIP) column is kept separately because it covers the pregnancy, not the woman's full Medicaid.

DC.note: Effective Jan 1, 2026 DC cut parents from 221% to 138% and other adults from 215% to 138% FPL and moved adults 138-200% FPL to the Healthy DC Plan (a Basic Health Program). For 2025 use parents 221, adultsNoKids 215 (KFF footnote).

FL.note: Florida did not answer the 2026 survey; KFF carried prior-year levels confirmed from public information.

GA.note: Not an ACA expansion state; covers parents and other adults to 100% FPL through the Pathways section 1115 waiver only if they meet a work requirement (KFF footnote).

IA.note: KFF footnote: pregnancy Medicaid limit cut from 375% to 215% FPL (table value shown is 220); infant upper limit cut from 380% to 307% effective Jan 1, 2025.

MI.note: Covers pregnant people and children up to 400% FPL affected by the Flint water crisis (not reflected in the figures).

MN.note: Basic Health Program (MinnesotaCare) covers adults 138-200% FPL (KFF footnote).

NV.note: Pregnancy limit raised from 190% to 205% FPL effective July 1, 2025.

NY.note: Essential Plan (Basic Health Program) covers adults 138-250% FPL (KFF footnote).

OR.note: Basic Health Program covers adults 138-200% FPL (KFF footnote).

TX.note: Parent limit is for a single-parent family of three; based on monthly dollar amounts (KFF footnote).

VA.note: Section 1931 parent limit varies by region; value is region 2 (KFF footnote).

WI.note: Not an ACA expansion state; covers adults to 100% FPL in regular Medicaid (KFF footnote).

medicaidNationalMedians2026.note: KFF 'United States' row = median across states.

medicaidRulesNotes: Values are January 2026. Changes between 2025 and January 2026 that KFF footnotes: DC adults/parents (see DC note). Others listed in state notes are earlier changes. No state changed ACA expansion status in 2024-2026.

In non-expansion states, adultsNoKids is null: no full Medicaid for non-disabled, non-pregnant adults without dependent children at any income (except GA's work-requirement waiver and WI's 100% coverage).
Disabled and 65+ Medicaid eligibility (SSI-related, medically needy, Medicare Savings Programs) is not in these tables.
Immigration status rules (5-year bar for many lawful immigrants; undocumented ineligible for full Medicaid) apply on top of income limits and are not in these tables.

territories.summary: Territories are treated as states for Medicaid except that federal funding is capped each year (Section 1108(g) allotment, grown by medical CPI-U), the federal match (FMAP) is set in statute (55% in the 2021 fact sheet, temporarily raised by later laws), and they may set eligibility by a measure other than the FPL. HHS poverty guidelines are not defined for Puerto Rico or other outlying jurisdictions (FR 2024).

PR.incomeStandard: Puerto Rico local poverty level (set by state plan amendment)
PR.acaAdultGroup: Adopted, up to 133% of local poverty level
PR.chip: Medicaid-expansion CHIP; only territory using CHIP for children above regular Medicaid limits

GU.acaAdultGroup: Adopted, up to 133% of local poverty level

VI.acaAdultGroup: Adopted, up to 133% of local poverty level

AS.incomeStandard: No individual eligibility or enrollment. Federal funds pay for care in proportion to the share of the population below 200% FPL (presumptive method under a Section 1902(j) waiver).

MP.incomeStandard: SSI income and asset standards (CNMI is the only territory in SSI); Section 1902(j) waiver

section1108AllotmentsMillions.note: FY2020-21 were raised by P.L. 116-94 and FFCRA (PR about $2.7-2.8 billion). Later laws changed funding again; not researched here.

povertyGuidelines2024.formula: guideline(n) = base1Person + perAdditionalPerson * (n - 1); exact for every size in the 2024 tables
povertyGuidelines2024.territories: Not defined for Puerto Rico or other outlying jurisdictions; each federal program decides (FR text).

context2026.note: 2026 contiguous-state figures quoted in the KFF notes; the KFF percentages are relative to these.

employerCoverage.universe: Private-sector establishments and their employees; firm size counts employees of the whole firm.
employerCoverage.definitions: eligibleShare = % of employees in offering establishments who are eligible; takeUp = % of eligible employees who enroll; enrolledShare = % of all employees in offering establishments who enroll (= eligible x takeUp). 'Percent low-wage employees' group in the characteristic tables uses MEPS-IC's low-wage definition (an hourly wage cutoff set by MEPS-IC each year).

offerByState.note: Private-sector, all firm sizes unless named. Small-state subgroup values can carry wide errors; check the source sheet's '*' (relative SE > 30%) markers before relying on a firm-size cell.

acs2023.measure: coverage at time of interview; types alone or in combination

cpsAsec2024_forCY2023.measure: uninsured = no coverage all calendar year; types = any time in year

cpsAsec2024_forCY2023.note: P60-284 Table A-1/A-2 give private/public by age, not each subtype by age.

uninsuredByState.fields: all = percent uninsured all ages (moe = 90% margin); under19, age19to64, age65plus; below138FPL = all ages below 138% of poverty threshold; pop = civilian noninstitutionalized

acs2023_19to64.note: Computed from counts. Coverage-type shares overlap.

cpsAsec2024_19to64_byExpansion.note: Expansion status as of Jan 1, 2023 (NC and SD counted as non-expansion). Nonexpansion below-100% estimate rests on a small sample (P60 text).

acs2023.note: countUnder65 = under-19 + 19-64 counts from S2704 (sum computed here).

medicare.under65Rule: People under 65 get Medicare after receiving Social Security Disability Insurance for 24 months (after a 5-month wait for the cash benefit, so about 29 months after disability onset); the waiting period is waived for ALS. People with end-stage renal disease also qualify. (Trustees Report glossary.)
medicare.eligibilityAt65: Most people qualify at 65 through their own or a spouse's work record (not separately sourced here).

gaps: Medicaid limits are KFF's January 2026 snapshot; the live KFF pages no longer publish the January 2025 timeframe and the Wayback Machine was unreachable. The only 2025-to-2026 change KFF footnotes for adults/parents is DC (2025: parents 221, adults 215). Some small child/pregnancy changes during 2025 may not be footnoted.
CMS Medicaid.gov eligibility table is dated December 1, 2023 and leaves out the 5% disregard, so it was not used for values.

Territories: no current income limits as % of FPL. Local poverty levels for PR, GU and VI are set by state plan amendment and were not found in a federal table. MACPAC fact sheet is February 2021; section 1108 funding and PR's eligibility have changed since (e.g., later appropriations laws) and were not researched. ACS gives a PR uninsured rate (5.3%) but no ACS 1-year for other territories.

MEPS-IC offer rates are for private-sector employers only. Public-sector (state and local government) employer data exists in the MEPS-IC 'Public' export and was not extracted. Federal employees not covered.

MEPS-IC state values: only the four headline measures by state were extracted (all firm sizes, under/over 50). Firm-size cells for small states are often marked unreliable ('*') or suppressed in the source; flags are kept in scratch extract meps_state_extract.json but not carried into this file except via the warning.
Uninsured by income-to-poverty for 19-64 by state was not pulled (B27016 by state is available from the same API).

ACS and CPS measure different things (point-in-time vs full-year uninsured; ACS 'direct-purchase' is higher than CPS because of reporting differences). Check a simulation against one source consistently.
No source here gives employer-coverage take-up as a function of household income or of a spouse's coverage; MEPS-IC gives take-up by establishment wage mix only ('Percent low-wage employees').
Marketplace subsidy rules (premium tax credits 100/138-400% FPL, enhanced credits through 2025, family glitch fix) and immigration-status rules were out of scope and not sourced.

Medicare: the Trustees 'disabled' count is under-65 entitlement and may include ESRD-only beneficiaries; a separate SSDI-only Medicare count was not pulled (CMS Program Statistics 'Medicare Total Enrollment' tables have it by entitlement reason).
